day.title: Tuesday after the Nineteenth Sunday after Trinity

The first lesson is appointed in the Calendar with the Table of Lessons (or the Table of Proper Lessons), which is not in the supplied source. No Scripture translation has been chosen for Lux yet.
The second lesson is appointed in the Calendar with the Table of Lessons (or the Table of Proper Lessons), which is not in the supplied source. No Scripture translation has been chosen for Lux yet.
The Jubilate is said instead of the Benedictus when the Benedictus is read in the second lesson. The lessons are not available, so this cannot be checked.

rubric.text: At the beginning of Morning Prayer the Minister ſhall read with a loud voice one or more of theſe Sentences of the Scriptures that follow. And then he ſhall ſay that which is written after the ſaid Sentences.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: WHEN the wicked man turneth away from his wickedneſs that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right, he ſhall ſave his ſoul alive.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: I acknowledge my tranſgreſſions; and my ſin is ever before me.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Hide thy face from my ſins, and blot out all mine iniquities.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: The ſacrifices of God are a broken ſpirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not deſpiſe.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, ſlow to anger, and of great kindneſs, and repenteth him of the evil.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveneſs, though we have rebelled against him: neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws which he ſet before us.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O Lord, correct me, but with judgment; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: I will ariſe and go to my father; and will ſay unto him, Father, I have ſinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy ſon.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Enter not into judgment with thy ſervant, O Lord; for in thy ſight ſhall no man living be juſtified.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: If we ſay that we have no ſin, we deceive ourſelves, and the truth is not in us: But if we confeſs our ſins, God is faithful and just to forgive us our ſins, and to cleanſe us from all unrighteouſneſs.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: DEARLY beloved brethren, the Scripture moveth us, in ſundry places, to acknowledge and confeſs our manifold ſins and wickedneſs; and that we ſhould not diſſemble nor cloke them before the face of Almighty God our heavenly Father; but confeſs them with an humble, lowly, penitent, and obedient heart; to the end that we may obtain forgiveneſs of the ſame, by his infinite goodneſs and mercy. And although we ought, at all times, humbly to acknowledge our ſins before God; yet ought we most chiefly ſo to do, when we aſſemble and meet together, to render thanks for the great benefits that we have received at his hands, to ſet forth his most worthy praiſe, to hear his most holy Word, and to aſk thoſe things that are requiſite and neceſſary, as well for the body as the ſoul. Wherefore I pray and beſeech you, as many as are here preſent, to accompany me, with a pure heart, and humble voice, unto the throne of the heavenly grace, ſaying after me:

rubric.text: A general Confeſſion to be ſaid of the whole Congregation, after the Minister, all kneeling.

text.speaker: all
text.text: ALMIGHTY and most merciful Father, We have erred and strayed from thy ways like lost ſheep: We have followed too much the devices and deſires of our own hearts: We have offended against thy holy laws: We have left undone thoſe things which we ought to have done; And we have done thoſe things which we ought not to have done; And there is no health in us. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us, miſerable offenders: Spare thou them, O God, which confeſs their fault: Restore thou them that are penitent; According to thy promiſes declared unto mankind in Christ Jeſu our Lord. And grant, O most merciful Father, for his ſake, That we may hereafter live a godly, righteous, and ſober life, To the glory of thy holy Name. Amen.

rubric.text: The Absolution or Remiſſion of ſins, to be pronounced by the Priest alone, standing; the People still kneeling.

text.speaker: priest
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, the Father of our Lord Jeſus Christ, who deſireth not the death of a ſinner, but rather that he may turn from his wickedneſs and live; and hath given power and commandment, to his Ministers, to declare and pronounce to his people, being penitent, the abſolution and remiſſion of their ſins: He pardoneth and abſolveth all them that truly repent, and unfeignedly believe his holy Goſpel. Wherefore let us beſeech him to grant us true repentance, and his Holy Spirit; that thoſe things may pleaſe him which we do at this preſent, and that the reſt of our life hereafter may be pure and holy; ſo that at the last we may come to his eternal joy; through Jeſus Christ our Lord.

rubric.text: The people ſhall anſwer here, and at the end of all other prayers,

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: Amen.

rubric.text: Then, the Minister ſhall kneel, and ſay the Lord’s Prayer with an audible voice: the people alſo kneeling, and repeating it with him, both here, and whereſoever elſe it is uſed in Divine Service.

text.speaker: all
text.text: OUR Father, which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven: Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our treſpaſſes, as we forgive them that treſpaſs againſt us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

rubric.text: Then likewiſe he ſhall ſay,

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, open thou our lips;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And our mouth ſhall ſhew forth thy praiſe.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O God, make ſpeed to ſave us.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: O Lord, make haste to help us.

rubric.text: Here all standing up, the Priest ſhall ſay,

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son: and to the Holy Ghost;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be: world without end. Amen.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Praiſe ye the Lord.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: The Lord’s Name be praiſed.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be ſaid or ſung this Pſalm following; except on EasterDay, upon which another Anthem is appointed: and on the Nineteenth Day of every Month it is not to be read here, but in the ordinary courſe of the Pſalms.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: O Come, let us ſing unto the Lord
verses.second: let us heartily rejoice in the strength of our ſalvation.

verses.first: Let us come before his preſence with thanksgiving
verses.second: and ſhow ourſelves glad in him with pſalms.

verses.first: For the Lord is a great God
verses.second: and a great King above all gods.

verses.first: In his hands are all the corners of the earth
verses.second: and the strength of the hills is his alſo.

verses.first: The ſea is his, and he made it
verses.second: and his hands prepared the dry land.

verses.first: O come, let us worſhip and fall down
verses.second: and kneel before the Lord our Maker.

verses.first: For he is the Lord our God
verses.second: and we are the people of his pasture, and the ſheep of his hand.

verses.first: To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts
verses.second: as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderneſs;

verses.first: When your fathers tempted me
verses.second: proved me, and ſaw my works.

verses.first: Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and ſaid
verses.second: It is a people that do err in their hearts, for they have not known my ways.

verses.first: Unto whom I ſware in my wrath
verses.second: that they ſhould not enter into my rest.

rubric.text: Then ſhall follow the Pſalms in order as they be appointed; and at the end of every Pſalm throughout the Year, and likewiſe in the end of Benedicte, Benedictus, Magnificat, and Nunc dimittis, ſhall be repeated,

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: LET God ariſe, and let his enemies be ſcattered
verses.second: let them alſo that hate him flee before him.

verses.first: Like as the ſmoke vaniſheth, ſo ſhalt thou drive them away
verses.second: and like as wax melteth at the fire, ſo let the ungodly periſh at the preſence of God.

verses.first: But let the righteous be glad and rejoice before God
verses.second: let them alſo be merry and joyful .

verses.first: O ſing unto God, and ſing praiſes unto his Name
verses.second: magnify him that rideth upon the heavens, as it were upon an horſe; praiſe him in his Name JAH, and rejoice before him.

verses.first: He is a father of the fatherleſs, and defendeth the cauſe of the widows
verses.second: even God in his holy habitation.

verses.first: He is the God that maketh men to be of one mind in an houſe, and bringeth the priſoners out of captivity
verses.second: but letteth the runagates continue in ſcarceneſs.

verses.first: O God, when thou wenteſt forth before the people
verses.second: when thou wenteſt through the wilderneſs;

verses.first: The earth ſhook, and the heavens dropped at the preſence of God
verses.second: even as Sinai alſo was moved at the preſence of God, who is the God of Iſrael.

verses.first: Thou, O God, ſenteſt a gracious rain upon thine inheritance
verses.second: and refreſhedſt it when it was weary.

verses.first: Thy congregation ſhall dwell therein
verses.second: for thou, O God, haſt of thy goodneſs prepared for the poor.

verses.first: The Lord gave the word
verses.second: great was the company of the preachers.

verses.first: Kings with their armies did flee, and were diſcomfited
verses.second: and they of the houſehold divided the ſpoil.

verses.first: Though ye have lien among the pots, yet ſhall ye be as the wings of a dove
verses.second: that is covered with ſilver wings, and her feathers like gold.

verses.first: When the Almighty ſcattered kings for their ſake
verses.second: then were they as white as ſnow in Salmon.

verses.first: As the hill of Baſan, ſo is God’s hill
verses.second: even an high hill, as the hill of Baſan.

verses.first: Why hop ye ſo, ye high hills? this is God’s hill, in the which it pleaſeth him to dwell
verses.second: yea, the Lord will abide in it for ever.

verses.first: The chariots of God are twenty thouſand, even thouſands of angels
verses.second: and the Lord is among them, as in the holy place of Sinai.

verses.first: Thou art gone up on high, thou haſt led captivity captive, and received gifts for men
verses.second: yea, even for thine enemies, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

verses.first: Praiſed be the Lord daily
verses.second: even the God who helpeth us, and poureth his benefits upon us.

verses.first: He is our God, even the God of whom cometh ſalvation
verses.second: God is the Lord, by whom we eſcape death.

verses.first: God ſhall wound the head of his enemies
verses.second: and the hairy ſcalp of ſuch a one as goeth on ſtill in his wickedneſs.

verses.first: The Lord hath ſaid, I will bring my people again, as I did from Baſan
verses.second: mine own will I bring again, as I did ſometime from the deep of the ſea.

verses.first: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies
verses.second: and that the tongue of thy dogs may be red through the ſame.

verses.first: It is well ſeen, O God, how thou goeſt
verses.second: how thou, my God and King, goeſt in the ſanctuary.

verses.first: The ſingers go before, the minſtrels follow after
verses.second: in the midſt are the damſels playing with the timbrels.

verses.first: Give thanks, O Iſrael, unto God the Lord in the congregations
verses.second: from the ground of the heart.

verses.first: There is little Benjamin their ruler, and the princes of Judah their counſel
verses.second: the princes of Zabulon, and the princes of Nephthali.

verses.first: Thy God hath ſent forth ſtrength for thee
verses.second: ſtabliſh the thing, O God, that thou haſt wrought in us,

verses.first: For thy temple’s ſake at Jeruſalem
verses.second: ſo ſhall kings bring preſents unto thee.

verses.first: When the company of the ſpear-men, and multitude of the mighty are ſcattered abroad among the beaſts of the people, ſo that they humbly bring pieces of ſilver
verses.second: and when he hath ſcattered the people that delight in war;

verses.first: Then ſhall the princes come out of Eqypt; the Morians land ſhall ſoon ſtretch out her hands unto God.
Sing unto God, O ye kingdoms of the earth
verses.second: O ſing praiſes unto the Lord;

verses.first: Who ſitteth in the heavens over all from the beginning
verses.second: lo, he doth ſend out his voice, yea, and that a mighty voice.

verses.first: Aſcribe ye the power to God over Iſrael
verses.second: his worſhip and ſtrength is in the clouds.

verses.first: O God, wonderful art thou in thy holy places
verses.second: even the God of Iſrael, he will give ſtrength and power unto his people; bleſſed be God.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be read distinctly with an audible voice the first Leſſon, taken out of the Old Testament, as it is appointed in the Calendar (except there be proper Leſſons aſſigned for that Day:) he that readeth ſo standing, and turning himſelf, as he may be heard of all ſuch as are preſent. And after that, ſhall be ſaid or ſung in Engliſh, the Hymn called Te Deum Laudamus daily throug-out the year.
Note, That before every Leſſon the Minister ſhall ſay, Here beginneth ſuch a Chapter, or Verſe of ſuch a Chapter, of ſuch a Book: And after every Leſſon, Here endeth the Firſt, or the Second Leſſon.

alternatives.label: Te Deum Laudamus or Benedicite, omnia opera.

verses.first: WE praiſe thee, O God
verses.second: we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.

verses.first: All the earth doth worſhip thee
verses.second: the Father everlaſting.

verses.first: To thee all Angels cry aloud
verses.second: the Heavens and all the Powers therein;

verses.first: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim
verses.second: continually do cry,

verses.first: Holy, Holy, Holy
verses.second: Lord God of Sabaoth;

verses.first: Heaven and earth are full of the Majesty
verses.second: of thy Glory.

verses.first: The glorious company of the Apostles
verses.second: praiſe thee.

verses.first: The goodly fellowſhip of the Prophets
verses.second: praiſe thee.

verses.first: The noble army of Martyrs
verses.second: praiſe thee.

verses.first: The holy Church throughout all the world
verses.second: doth acknowledge thee;

verses.first: The Father
verses.second: of an infinite Majesty;

verses.first: Thine adorable, true
verses.second: and only Son;

verses.first: Alſo the Holy Ghost
verses.second: the Comforter.

verses.first: Thou art the King of Glory
verses.second: O Christ.

verses.first: Thou art the everlasting Son
verses.second: of the Father.

verses.first: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man
verses.second: thou didst not abhor the Virgin’s womb.

verses.first: When thou hadst overcome the ſharpneſs of death
verses.second: thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

verses.first: Thou ſittest at the right hand of God
verses.second: in the glory of the Father.

verses.first: We believe that thou ſhalt come
verses.second: to be our Judge.

verses.first: We therefore pray thee, help thy ſervants
verses.second: whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious blood.

verses.first: Make them to be numbered with thy ſaints
verses.second: in glory everlasting.

verses.first: O Lord, ſave thy people
verses.second: and bleſs thine heritage.

verses.first: Govern them
verses.second: and lift them up for ever.

verses.first: Day by day
verses.second: we magnify thee;

verses.first: And we worſhip thy Name ever
verses.second: world without end.

verses.first: Vouchſafe, O Lord
verses.second: to keep us this day without ſin.

verses.first: O Lord, have mercy upon us
verses.second: have mercy upon us.

verses.first: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us
verses.second: as our trust is in thee.

verses.first: O Lord, in thee have I trusted
verses.second: let me never be confounded.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: O All ye Works of the Lord, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Angels of the Lord, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Heavens, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Waters that be above the firmament, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O all ye Powers of the Lord, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Sun and Moon, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Stars of heaven, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Showers and Dew, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Winds of God, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Fire and Heat, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Winter and Summer, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Dews and Froſts, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Frost and Cold, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Ice and Snow, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Nights and Days, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Light and Darkneſs, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Lightnings and Clouds, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O let the Earth bleſs the Lord
verses.second: yea, let it praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Mountains and Hills, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O all ye Green things upon the earth, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Wells, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Seas and Floods, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Whales, and all that move in the waters, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O all ye Fowls of the air, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O all ye Beasts and Cattle, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Children of men, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O let Iſrael bleſs the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Priests of the Lord, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Servants of the Lord, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Spirits and Souls of the righteous, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O ye Holy and Humble men of heart, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

verses.first: O Ananias, Azarias, and Miſael, bleſs ye the Lord
verses.second: praiſe him, and magnify him for ever.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be read in like manner the Second Leſſon, taken out of the New Testament: and after that, the Hymn following; except when that ſhall happen to be read in the Chapter for the day, or for the goſpel on St. John Baptist’s Day.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now
gloria.second: and ever ſhall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.first: BLESSED be the Lord God of Iſrael
verses.second: for he hath viſited and redeemed his people;

verses.first: And he hath raiſed up a mighty ſalvation for us
verses.second: in the houſe of his ſervant David;

verses.first: As he ſpoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets
verses.second: which have been ſince the world began;

verses.first: That we ſhould be ſaved from our enemies
verses.second: and from the hand of all that hate us;

verses.first: To perform the mercy promiſed to our forefathers
verses.second: and to remember his holy covenant;

verses.first: To perform the oath which he ſware to our forefather Abraham
verses.second: that he would give us;

verses.first: That we being delivered out of the hands of our enemies
verses.second: might ſerve him without fear;

verses.first: In holineſs and righteouſneſs before him
verses.second: all the days of our life.

verses.first: And thou, child, ſhalt be called the Prophet of the Highest
verses.second: for thou ſhalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways;

verses.first: To give knowledge of ſalvation unto his people
verses.second: for the remiſſion of their ſins,

verses.first: Through the tender mercy of our God
verses.second: whereby the Day-ſpring from on high hath viſited us;

verses.first: To give light to them that ſit in darkneſs, and in the ſhadow of death
verses.second: to guide our feet into the way of peace.

rubric.text: Or this Pſalm.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: O Be joyful in the Lord, all ye lands
verses.second: ſerve the Lord with gladneſs, and come before his preſence with a ſong.

verses.first: Be ye ſure that the Lord, he is God; it is he who hath made us, and not we ourſelves
verses.second: we are hiſ people, and the ſheep of his pasture.

verses.first: O go your way into his gates with thankſgiving, and into his courts with praiſe
verses.second: be thankful unto him, and ſpeak good of his Name.

verses.first: For the Lord is gracious, his mercy is everlasting
verses.second: and his truth endureth from generation to generation.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be ſung or ſaid the Apostles Creed, by the Minister and the People, standing: except only ſuch days as the Creed of St. Athanaſius is appointed to be read.

text.speaker: all
text.text: I Believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth: And in Jeſus Christ his only Son, our Lord; Who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, Born of the Virgin Mary, Suffered under Pontius Pilate, Was crucified, dead, and buried; He deſcended into hell; The third day he roſe again from the dead; He aſcended into heaven, And ſitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; From thence he ſhall come to judge the quick and the dead. I believe in the Holy Ghost; The holy Catholick Church; The Communion of Saints; The Forgiveneſs of ſins; The Reſurrection of the body; And the Life everlasting. Amen.

rubric.text: And after that theſe Prayers following, all devoutly kneeling; the Minister firſt pronouncing with a loud voice,

lines.speaker: minister
lines.text: The Lord be with you;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And with thy ſpirit.

rubric.text: Minister.

lines.speaker: minister
lines.text: Let us pray.

rubric.text: Then the Minister, Clerks, and People, ſhall ſay the Lord’s Prayer with a loud voice.

text.speaker: all
text.text: OUR Father, which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done, in earth as it is in heaven: Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our treſpaſſes, as we forgive them that treſpaſs against us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. Amen.

rubric.text: Then the Priest standing up, ſhall ſay,

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſhow thy mercy upon us;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And grant us thy ſalvation.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſave the King.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And mercifully hear us, when we call upon thee.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Endue thy Ministers with righteouſneſs;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And make thy choſen people joyful.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſave thy people;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And bleſs thine inheritance.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Give peace in our time, O Lord;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: Becauſe there is none other that fighteth for us, but only thou, O God.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O God, make clean our hearts within us;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And take not thy Holy Spirit from us.

rubric.text: Then ſhall follow three Collects: The first of the Day, which ſhall be the ſame that is appointed at the Communion; The ſecond for Peace: The third for Grace to live well: And the two last Collects ſhall never alter, but daily be ſaid at Morning Prayer throughout all the year, as followeth, all kneeling.

heading.text: The Collect of the Day: The Nineteenth Sunday after Trinity

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O God, foraſmuch as without thee we are not able to pleaſe thee; Mercifully grant, that thy Holy Spirit may in all things direct W O and rule our hearts; through Jeſus Chriſt our Lord. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O God, who art the author of peace and lover of concord, in knowledge of whom standeth our eternal life, whoſe ſervice is perfect freedom; Defend us thy humble ſervants in all aſſaults of our enemies; that we, ſurely trusting in thy defence, may not fear the power of any adverſaries, through the might of Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who haſt ſafely brought us to the beginning of this day; Defend us in the ſame with thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no ſin, neither run into any kind of danger; but that all our doings, being ordered by thy government, may be righteous in thy ſight; through Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

rubric.text: In Quires an Places where they ſing, here followeth the Anthem.
Then theſe five Prayers following are to be read here, except when the Litany is read; and then only the two last are to be read, as they are there placed.

heading.text: A Prayer for the King’s Majesty

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O Lord, our heavenly Father, high and mighty, King of kings, Lord of lords, the only Ruler of princes, who dost from thy throne behold all the dwellers upon earth; Most heartily we beſeech thee, with thy favor to behold our moſt gracious Sovereign Lord, King G EORGE ; and ſo repleniſh him with the grace of thy Holy Spirit, that he may alway incline to thy will, and walk in thy way: Endue him plenteouſly with heavenly gifts; grant him in health and wealth long to live; strengthen him that he may vanquiſh and overcome all his enemies, and finally, after this life he may attain everlasting joy and felicity; through Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

heading.text: A Prayer for the Royal Family

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, the fountain of all goodneſs, we humbly beſeech thee to bleſs our gracious Queen C HARLOTTE , her Royal Highneſs the Princeſs Dowager of Wales, and all the Royal Family: Endue them with thy Holy Spirit; enrich them with thy heavenly grace; proſper them with all happineſs; and bring them to thine everlaſting kingdom; through Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

heading.text: A Prayer for the Clergy and People.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY and everlaſting God, who alone workest great marvels; Send down upon our Biſhops and Curates, and all Congregations committed to their charge, the healthful Spirit of thy grace; and that they may truly pleaſe thee, pour upon them the continual dew of thy bleſſing: Grant this, O Lord, for the honour of our Advocate and Mediator, Jeſus Christ. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, who hast given us grace at this time with one accord to make our common ſupplications unto thee; and dost promiſe that when two or three are gathered together in thy Name thou wilt grant their requests; Fulfill now, O Lord, the deſires and petitions of thy ſervants, as may be most expedient for them; granting us in this world knowledge of thy truth, and in the world to come life everlasting. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: THE grace of our Lord Jeſus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowſhip of the Holy Ghost, be with us all evermore. Amen.

rubric.text: Here endeth the Order of Morning Prayer throughout the Year.
